primaryContext.title: Street Fighter 6 Character Guide | Arjun
primaryContext.note: The official guide’s embedded English text and animations were reviewed for Arm of Justice, Cruel Shoulder, Breathing Ring/Shockwave, Divine Pillar, Justice Beyond, Ghastly Interrogation, Indomitable Defense/Moral Breakdown and the three Supers. Justice Beyond automatically grabs and swings the Pillar after Shoulder contact; it is not a command grab on the defender. Pillar hold delays activation. Recoverable gray damage and the command throw’s change with existing gray health are distinct from a stock/install system. Actual practice excerpts use the independent tutorials’ visible commands, HUD and results.

interpretationDecisions.decision: The light-to-command-grab take contains cr.LK, cr.LP, st.LP, a three-bar Rush cancel, st.LP and light command grab. It is not raw Rush. The CH low/medium take continues through st.HK target and Level 1. Commas in other overlays identify alternative specials, not one chain. Two more unclear Rush-caption candidates remain excluded pending exact follow-up.

Live cyan/light, yellow/medium and red/heavy button glyphs govern strengths. The printed standing-jab/medium-kick branch actually begins with cr.LP, confirmed by the down-plus-light-punch history and crouching attack animation. Arm follow-ups and the Mura heavy-kick/Pillar stance route preserve their actual 6HP. The Soul stance routes instead perform neutral HP after 22HK (hold), without an invented forward input. Four OD Pillar commands preserve their actual LK+MK or MK+HK pairs; no general pair-to-placement rule is inferred. Initial setup prerequisites/costs are separate from the performed follow-up. No stock/install is inferred.

Shoulder contact with the existing Pillar triggers an automatic club strike: Arjun grabs/swings the Pillar, not the defender. Ghastly Interrogation is a separate 63214LP command grab. Blocked Pillar/Shoulder pressure is not labeled a successful throw.
The held heavy Pillar delays activation. Held heavy-kick stance and Moral Breakdown are explicit. Source +F values are reported remaining advantage, not invented numerical wait commands.

The two selected grounded anti-airs cover Luke’s shown front/far jumps. The intervening cross-up and late Shoulder examples fail and limit that coverage. The corner Rush/jab-whiff feint guards only the recorded Ryu OD uppercut; the separate OD-Pillar/command-throw approach loses to an OD uppercut and is excluded from safety claims.

Oki tags cover the actual knockdown follow-ups. Anti-air tags belong to the two incoming-jump interceptions. Super use alone does not imply Cash-out. Large full-resource alternatives remain unprocessed, and no carry usefulness is inferred solely from an ender name.

remainingGaps: Substantial neutral, Arm pressure, Ring/projectile defense, Pillar/stance, DI/PC and full-resource alternatives remain available in the annotated source.
MC Mura has many additional Pillar/Rush-overhead, parry, reversal and Super examples requiring exact input/strength review; none is claimed exhausted.
Official context was reviewed, while its input-history-free practice execution remains unextracted.
